findings.evidence: focus.json stops 4 and 7: two links both named 'Premium' (one starred text link, one blue button); also a lone 'Learn More' link further down (dom CTRL list).

findings.evidence: Filter buttons at y4896 are plain <button>s; the active filter is shown by fill colour only and dom-1440.json records no role or pressed state.
findings.after: aria-pressed="true|false" on each chip inside role="group" aria-label="Filter demos"; announce 'Showing 6 of 39 demos' in an aria-live="polite" region
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value and 4.1.3 Status Messages. (Capture does not list aria-pressed; confirm in source.)

findings.evidence: '39 demos available • 20 categories • 26 light • 13 dark' distinguishes its terms only by colour (blue, orange, green) and the 'Light'/'Dark' badges on cards rely on white vs black fill; the colours carry no extra meaning, but the 'Colors:' swatch rows on each demo card present palettes as colour dots only with no text values.
findings.after: Add hex values as text or a title/aria-label per swatch ('#3B82F6 primary')
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.4.1 Use of Color and 1.1.1: palette information is available only visually.

findings.evidence: dom-1440.json: the h1 'UI UX Pro Max Design Intelligence' records empty own text and h2s are split into spans ('Supported' + gradient span, 'How It' + 'Works'); footer jumps h2 to h4 (sweep). The text is real, so this is a check item, not a failure, but headings built of gradient-clip spans can be read as separate words by some screen readers.
findings.after: Keep heading text in one node; apply the gradient with background-clip on the whole heading or drop it
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships, 2.4.6 Headings and Labels.
